title: cairn <device> start --new launches the instance the shim names
intention: cairn <device> start --new asks the shim which instance it would take, then launches <device>.<n> for that number through the dispatcher's existing instance routing, so a second instance is started on purpose, the dispatcher never computes the number, and a refusal from the shim stops the launch loudly.
why: Akien, outline 5.3.5.2.2 (said 2026-11-13): 'the launcher has to ask the shim to create the instance, and so it's the shim's job to say ... we have a cc_0 instance, so I'll launch it with cc_1'. The launcher asks, the shim names, the launcher launches (orchestrator ruling). --new as the flag for 'on purpose, I want another one' is CC's reading of Q#93, not his words. bin/cairn already routes cairn <device>[.<instance>].
traces_to: RULE 1 (the dispatcher talks to the shim through its public interface) and CP1.
how: Add --new to the dispatcher's start path: ask the shim (shim.name_instance, ticket d13859e2ae46) for the instance, then run the same routing as cairn <device>.<n> start. The ask mechanism is the build's first decision. Depends on d13859e2ae46 and 0f7a8cada1ca. superclaude is untouched.

clauses.claim: cairn <device> start --new with <device>_0 live asks the shim for the instance and launches <device>.<n> for the number the shim returns, leaving instance 0 untouched
when the shim refuses a name, the dispatcher exits non-zero with the refusal on stderr and launches nothing

decisions.text: D1: --new in bin/cairn's start path asks the shim for the name and then routes <device>.<n>.
D2: one proof on a scratch HOME, one tooth per clause; red first.

out: superclaude asking the cc shim instead of its own loop.pid/tmux check (ae4d581be071): a follow-on, not now
a device declaring whether it may have more than one instance: a follow-on, not built

measured.saw: bin/cairn's header documents cairn <device>[.<instance>] [verb] [args...], default instance 0; superclaude (cairn/devices/cc/superclaude 262-296) already moves a held instance to the next free one in bash; shim.py:1288 'start' starts only the instance the shim is. There is no generic --new.
